answer: A practical Sybil defense is per-identity bonding: a protocol lets an agent act only after it locks collateral in a contract, so a cluster of fake identities must post that stake for every head. When one member is caught colluding, the contract can slash siblings sharing a registration trail, so an attacker who tries to forge thousands of cheap wallets sees the bond price spiral upward with each detected batch. An identity that pays honestly stays as good as ivory, while the attacker's marginal cost per vote or reward is now locked capital that expected profit must beat.
